messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: KV cache size spike and streaming token cadence drop detected on prod-dedicated-1. Metric: kv_cache_bytes ~ +420% over 10m, continuous_batch_latency increased 3x, streaming_token_rate dropped ~60%. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

Alex (infra): copying logs, taking a look. which region? any customer-facing errors?

Mira (oncall): seeing increased 503s on streaming endpoints in eu-west-1. Support reports a few customers seeing stalled responses (no downstream tokens for 15-30s).

Tina (support): customer-phi reported: "tokens stopped mid-response, then full reconnect". Multiple tickets; severity P1 for impacted customers.

James (sre): first-pass hypothesis: continuous batching + aggressive KV prefetching caused cache blowup -> heavy GC + backpressure on streaming workers -> token cadence stalls / partial flushes.

Cleo (eng-ml): that matches an earlier repro where prefix prefetching under high concurrency created many ephemeral KV shards. If partial flush happens while batches are inflight we end up with orphaned KV entries and memory amplification.

Alex (infra): propose immediate mitigations (fast, reversible):
- reduce continuous_batch_window from 40ms -> 8ms
- disable kv_prefix_prefetch for prod-dedicated-1
- temporarily route new streaming sessions to fallback model variant (cpu-passthrough) for affected customers

Mira (oncall): prioritize reducing batch window and disabling prefetch. Who can push that config?

Alex (infra): I'm spinning up a config patch. patch below (will apply via k8s configmap roll):

```
# patch: reduce batch window and disable prefix prefetch
continuous_batch_window_ms: 8
kv_prefix_prefetch: false
kv_evict_threshold_pct: 0.82
```

Alex (infra): plan: apply to canary pool (2 nodes) -> monitor 60s -> roll to region if canary is good.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by Alex (infra) to prod-dedicated-1/canary. Rollout id: r-21004568-01

deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded (r-21004568-01). Health checks: ok.

Mira (oncall): after canary: kv_cache_bytes on canary nodes dropped ~55% within 2m, streaming token rate recovered to ~90% baseline. Good sign. Proceeding with region roll.

James (sre): rolling config to remaining nodes with a 20s stagger. Monitoring for partial flush errors in logs.

Cleo (eng-ml): note: this is a mitigation, not a root fix. We need a code patch to avoid orphaned KV entries on partial flush and add stronger backpressure when kv growth is detected. Filing a ticket.

Tina (support): updating customers: "We've applied a mitigation and are observing improved streaming stability. Engineering is investigating root cause; we'll share updates."

Alex (infra): completed region roll at +12m. Observed overall latency back to baseline and errors reduced to near-zero for affected tenants. Marking as mitigated.

Mira (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours. Next steps: tag for postmortem, severity review, and long-term engineering fix.

James (sre): quick follow-ups:
- create alert for sustained kv growth when continuous_batch_latency > 2x baseline (reduce noise)
- add emergency toggle for continuous batching per-tenant (fast fallbacks)
- health endpoint to detect partial flush occurrences (emit metric partial_flush_orphans)

Cleo (eng-ml): created GH issue: redwood/infra#4821 "partial flush orphaning under prefetch -> memory blowup". Initial PR draft to add safe-guarding around in-flight partial flushes.

Mira (oncall): timeline to include in postmortem. Recording timestamps and customer impact. Will hand to oncall+eng tomorrow for RCA.

Alex (infra): final note: if we see similar backpressure patterns in other regions, do not escalate to full failover immediately — first low-risk mitigation is to shrink batch window + disable prefetch, then consider tenant-level fallbacks.

Tina (support): customers A & B confirmed recovered behavior. Closing customer-facing alerts.

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated by Mira (oncall) at ts:2100456950. Please open postmortem and link any follow-up PRs. :white_check_mark:
